The Board adopted Resolution 21-081 honoring seventy-four 2022 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, accepted the district's audited 2021 financial statements presented by Plante Moran with no findings or questioned costs, and amended its 2021 tax rate request to comply with section 1211 hold-harmless limits under 2021 PA 48. The amended Form L-4029 sets a Principal Residence millage request of 3.3878 mills and a Non-Homestead operating request of 14.6122 mills.
2021_226_corrected_m101921bdmtg.page:
Meeting and Attendance
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, October 19, 2021, at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.; adjournment was at 8:57 p.m. Present with Mr. Schmidt were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson, plus Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, Carrier, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Fulcher, Brinks, Cottone, DiPonio, Godfrey, Whan and West. Approximately 90 members of the audience attended. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary; footers are marked "corrected JH."

Recognition
The TSD Mission Moment honored Hill Elementary School's schoolwide "Color Run" of Friday, October 1st, designed to be inclusive of students with sensory issues; Principal Shari Pawlus and her PTO board members received a certificate. Resolution 21-081 commended seventy-four 2022 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists; per the resolution, more than one million students nationwide from some 21,000 high schools entered the program and only 16,000 seniors are selected as semifinalists, by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT with comparable SAT scores. Copies were to be presented at a reception on November 3rd.

Actions Taken

| Res. | Item | Moved / Supported | Vote |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21-081 | 2022 National Merit Semifinalists resolution | — | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 21-082 | Consent agenda items A, B, C | Hauff / Gottlieb | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 21-083 | Accept audited 2021 financial statements | Wilson / Philippart | Yes 7, No 0 |
| 21-084 | Operating-All (Hold-Harmless) millage amendment | Philippart / Anne | Yes 7, No 0 |

Consent agenda 21-082 covered minutes of the September 7, 2021 Board Workshop, minutes of the September 21, 2021 Board Meeting, and the Treasurer's Report - August 2021.

Business
2020/2021 Audit: Ms. Donna Hanson and Mr. Michael Walsh of Plante Moran presented the audit of the 2020-2021 fiscal year, a draft of which had been detailed at the October 5, 2021 Board Workshop. There were no findings or questioned costs. Governmental funds revenue and expenditures, student population and foundation allowance were reviewed.

Millage amendment: The June 15, 2021 Budget Appropriations Resolution had authorized 4.4575 mills on Principal Residence, Qualified Agriculture, Qualified Forest and Industrial Personal Properties and 13.5425 mills on all Non-Homestead Properties, a total levy of 18 mills for general operating purposes. The FY22 state school aid act, 2021 PA 48 (HB 4411), reduces hold-harmless (OPR ALL) millage; under section 1211 of the state school code per-pupil hold-harmless revenue is limited to the difference between the district's foundation allowance and $8,700. The amended 2021 Tax Rate Request (Form L-4029) sets a Principal Residence request of 3.3878 mills, 1.1591 of them levied December 1, 2021, and a Non-Homestead operating request of 14.6122 mills, 7.8409 of them levied on the December 1, 2021 levy date, and goes to the Oakland County Clerk and City of Troy Clerk.

Public Comment and Reports
Non-agenda speakers were split between opposition to and support for the mask mandate and Covid protocols, with further comment on library books, parental rights, a Schroeder Elementary drop-off incident, the Covid Family Guidebook and the "Moms for Liberty" organization. Student representatives Yara Mashal (International Academy-East), Sasha Palmkoeck (Athens High School) and Sarayu Bethamcherla (Troy High School) reported; Alyssa McLarty (Troy College and Career High School) was not in attendance. Additions & Deletions, agenda-item public communication, Personnel and Curriculum were all "None."

Other
Board members congratulated Rick West and the Business Office for the audit. Dr. Machesky reported the Facilities Review Committee (FRC) held its first meeting, comprised of 54 community members and three Board members. Mr. Schmidt announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, November 9th at 6:00 p.m. and the next regular Board Meeting for Tuesday, November 16th at 7:00 p.m., both at the Services Building.
2021_226_corrected_m101921bdmtg.verbose:
Corrected minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, held October 19, 2021 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Every page footer carries the notation "Board of Education Meeting [page] October 19, 2021 - corrected JH," identifying this as the corrected version of the October 19 minutes. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist notation GH/jh.

Call to Order and Attendance
President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, Carrier, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Fulcher, Brinks, Cottone, DiPonio, Godfrey, Whan and West. There were approximately 90 members of the audience. The meeting adjourned at 8:57 p.m.

Recognition - TSD Mission Moment: Hill Elementary School "Color Run"
Hill Elementary students participated in a schoolwide Color Run event on Friday, October 1st. The Fun Run was specifically designed to be inclusive and mindful of students who might have sensory issues. The Color Run involves colorful chalk being thrown into the air and decorating the shirts of those running by, and Fun Runs typically involve lots of cheering, music, loud audio and visual stimulants. For a portion of Hill's Color Run the music was turned off and cheering consisted of hands in the air and thumbs up instead of clapping and raised voices; the quiet allowed students who have sensory issues to fully enjoy the Fun Run, and the entire 5th grade was there to quietly but enthusiastically cheer them on. The minutes characterize the event as an example of the district's Red Pillar (Equity & Well-Being) "at its finest," thanking Hill Elementary for demonstrating that "ALL means ALL in the TSD." The Board invited Principal Shari Pawlus up along with her PTO board members to receive a certificate of recognition.

Recognition and Resolution 21-081 - 2021-22 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists
The minutes state that more than one million students nationwide, from some 21,000 high schools, entered the National Merit Scholarship Program, but only 16,000 of these seniors are selected to be semifinalists. The Board passed a resolution to commend and congratulate the district's seventy-four National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, named as: Prisha Agnihotri, Frederick Aldinger, Sreenand Anumolu, Akshat Arya, Seo Hyun Baek, Cole Balintfy, Sarayu Bethamcherla, Shreya Bhargava, Kevin Chang, Sanya Chawla, Emily Chen, Reagan Choi, Shiham Chowdhury, Abhishek Dahad, Raaga Dandavolu, Atharva Dharphale, Malina Dumitrascu, Nikita Ganesh, Rittik Ghosh, Mariska Goswami, Navya Gullapuram, Albert Hua, Nicolas Hung, Jemi Isaac, Neha Jaisankar, Udayvir Jalf, Victoria Jan, Agastya Jayanthi, Sachin Karatha, Hyun Kim, Havesh Kolli, Rishi Konduru, Aileen Liu, Allison Liu, Aditi Locula, Iris Ma, Mlahat Mahmood, Meera Manek, Anay Modi, Brandon Nguyen, Abel Noble, Tanisha Panchal, Esha Patel, Avani Prasad, Ayush Pujara, Vandhana Purushothaman, Yahya Qamar, Eric Qiao, Katie Qu, Danny Samuel, Mohammad Shaik, Navya Shankar, Sanjana Sharma, Rishi Shetty, Heejin Shyn, Kishan Soni, Saakshi Sovani, Sachin Sridhar, Vidhya Harini Srinivas, Smriti Suresh, Dilan Swami, Sharanya Swaminathan, Areej Tahir, Jordan Tansingco, Cole VanAmberg, Rebecca Varghese, Akshay Vasudevan, Andrew Wang, Roger Wang, Claire Wu, Angela Xu, Gary Xu, Rachel Yang and Nancy Yao. The minutes call this a remarkable number of semifinalists and a tribute to the staff and parents of the Troy School District; copies of the resolution were to be presented to the students at a reception on November 3rd.

The resolution recites that student achievement is honored through the National Merit Scholarship semifinalist and finalist recognition programs, and that National Merit students reach semifinalist status by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the National Preliminary Scholastic Aptitude Test (PSAT) and earning comparable scores on the Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT). It resolves that the Troy School District Board of Education adopts the resolution in honor of the students for their selection as 2022 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists. The vote was Yes 7, No 0, recorded as item 21-081.

Additions & Deletions; Public Communication (Agenda Items)
Both were recorded as None.

General - Consent Agenda, Resolution 21-082
It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Gottlieb that the Troy Board of Education take action to approve items A, B and C on the consent agenda: (A) Minutes of the September 7, 2021 Board of Education Workshop; (B) Minutes of the September 21, 2021 Board of Education Meeting; and (C) Treasurer's Report - August 2021. The vote was Yes 7, No 0.

Personnel and Curriculum
Both sections were recorded as None.

Business - 2020/2021 Audit Report, Resolution 21-083
Ms. Donna Hanson and Mr. Michael Walsh from Plante Moran provided a presentation to the Board of Education on the audit of the 2020-2021 fiscal year. A draft copy of the District's Audit Report had been presented in detail to the Board at the October 5, 2021 Board Workshop. Ms. Hanson and Mr. Walsh provided highlights of the audit and shared that there were no findings or questioned costs. Governmental funds revenue and expenditures were reviewed, as were student population and foundation allowance. The economic impact of the pandemic challenges, as well as the changes in federal funding, was also discussed at length. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Board of Education accept and approve the Troy School District's audited 2021 financial statements as presented by Plante Moran. The vote was Yes 7, No 0.

Business - 2021-2022 Amendment of the Operating-All (Hold-Harmless) Millage, Resolution 21-084
It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne. The resolution recites that the Board, pursuant to a 2021-22 Budget Appropriations Resolution adopted on June 15, 2021, approved the School District's operating, debt and sinking fund millage rates for the 2021-22 school year, which included the authority to levy 4.4575 mills on Principal Residence, Qualified Agriculture, Qualified Forest and Industrial Personal Properties and 13.5425 mills on all Non-Homestead Properties for a total levy of 18 mills for general operating purposes. It further recites that the FY 22 state school aid act, 2021 PA 48, HB 4411, reduces the amount of hold harmless (OPR ALL) millage districts may levy in 2021 for FY 22; that under section 1211 of the state school code the per pupil hold-harmless revenue is limited to the difference between the district's foundation allowance and $8,700; and that the Board desires to comply with section 1211 of the FY22 state school aid act.

The Board resolved to approve an amendment to the 2021-22 Budget Appropriations Resolution to approve and authorize the School District to modify the Principal Residence, Qualified Agriculture, Qualified Forest and Industrial Personal and the Non-Homestead Properties millage rate levies for a total levy of 18 mills for general operating purposes. It further resolved to authorize the President and Secretary to sign an amended 2021 Tax Rate Request (Form L-4029) with a Principal Residence, Qualified Agriculture, Qualified Forest and Industrial Personal Properties millage request of 3.3878, with 1.1591 mills of the 3.3878 to be levied on December 1, 2021, and a Non-Homestead operating millage request of 14.6122, with 7.8409 mills of the 14.6122 mills to be levied on the December 1, 2021 levy date, and that the amended 2021 Tax Rate Request be submitted to the Oakland County Clerk and City of Troy Clerk. The vote was Yes 7, No 0.

Reports from Student Representatives to the Board
Yara Mashal, student representative for International Academy-East; Sasha Palmkoeck, student representative for Athens High School; and Sarayu Bethamcherla, student representative for Troy High School, each shared a report on events and activities happening in their schools. Alyssa McLarty, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, was not in attendance.

Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items)
President Schmidt shared a statement providing the structure of how the evening's Public Participation would be conducted in compliance with the Open Meetings Act and reviewed the guidelines for public comment. Speakers were: Carrie Leser, TSD parent, on a concerning incident occurring at Schroeder Elementary School during morning drop-off and how it is confusing students; Diana Magiera, TSD parent, in opposition to the mask-wearing mandate; Fabrice Smielianskas, TSD parent, in support of the Covid protocols put in place in the district; Ollie Apahidean, TSD parent, on parental rights, displaying pictures from a book found in the school library; Ana Maria Gould, TSD parent, in support of mask-wearing in schools; Yousef Safah, Co-Founder of Mind Matters Education, on mental health support for students; B.J. Lennon, TSD parent, in opposition to the mask mandate; Ashleigh Jennings, TSD parent, in support of the mask mandate; Kacy Bailey, TSD parent, introducing "Moms for Liberty," an Oakland County organization she represents to defend parental rights; Ryan Johnson, TSD parent, in opposition to the mask mandate and expressing concerns of unlawful activities happening; Kelly Jones, TSD parent, in support of the mask mandate; Sarah Krieger, TSD parent, in opposition to the mask mandate; Peggy Chinoski, TSD parent, in support of the mask mandate; and Thomas Fraser, TSD parent, on the recently published Covid Family Guidebook related to quarantine restrictions for students.

Other
Board members congratulated Rick West and his team in the Business Office for the great audit report and their fiscal stewardship, and congratulated the National Merit Semi-Finalists for their accomplishments. Dr. Machesky shared that the Facilities Review Committee (FRC) kicked off its first meeting; the team is comprised of 54 community members and three Board members. He also shared that the Fall Update presentations had begun to building staff and PTOs. Mr. Schmidt shared that the next Board Workshop would be held on Tuesday, November 9th at 6:00 p.m. at the Services Building and the next regular Board Meeting would be Tuesday, November 16th at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building.

Adjournment
The meeting adjourned at 8:57 p.m.

Meeting and Attendance
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, November 16, 2021, at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; adjournment was at 8:38 p.m. Present with Mr. Schmidt were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson, plus Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Detmer, Morey and West. Approximately 85 members of the audience attended. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (GH/jh).

Recognitions
TSD Mission Moment: Troy High School senior Reagan Choi was recognized for a perfect score on the AP Physics C: Mechanics Exam in May 2021. AP Exams are scored on a scale of 1 to 5; Reagan received the top score of 5 and, per the minutes, is "in the 0.00% in the world for an absolute perfect score," one of only two students in the world who answered every single question perfectly. Actions Taken

| Res. | Item | Moved / Supported | Vote |

2021_227_m111621bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, held November 16, 2021 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist notation GH/jh.

Call to Order and Attendance
President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Detmer, Morey and West. There were approximately 85 members of the audience. The meeting adjourned at 8:38 p.m.

Recognition - TSD Mission Moment: THS Student Receives Perfect Score on AP Physics Exam
The Board recognized Troy High School senior Reagan Choi for receiving a perfect score on the AP Physics C: Mechanics Exam in May 2021. The minutes note that Reagan's performance was so superior that it fell into an extremely select category; Advanced Placement Exams are college-level examinations scored on a scale of 1 to 5, and Reagan not only received the top score of 5 but is "in the 0.00% in the world for an absolute perfect score." He is one of only two students in the world who answered every single question perfectly. The Board invited teacher Brian Glynn to introduce Reagan and share his accomplishment; Reagan received congratulations from the Board along with a certificate.

Recognition - 2021-22 National Blue Ribbon Awards: Barnard & Leonard Elementary Schools
The Board recognized Barnard Elementary School and Leonard Elementary School for their designation as National Blue-Ribbon Schools, an award honoring them as among the very best schools in the United States. Barnard and Leonard were recognized by U.S. Secretary of Education Miguel Cardona at a ceremony in Washington, D.C. on November 4th and 5th. Only 325 schools from around the country were chosen for this honor in 2021. The minutes state the award affirms the hard work of students, staff, parents and the Barnard and Leonard communities, and quote Secretary Cardona: "This year's cohort of honorees demonstrates what is possible when committed educators and school leaders create vibrant, welcoming, and affirming school cultures where rich teaching and learning can flourish," and "I commend our Blue-Ribbon honorees for working to keep students healthy and safe while meeting their academic, social, emotional, and mental health needs. In the face of unprecedented circumstances, you found creative ways to engage, care for, protect, and teach our children. Blue Ribbon Schools have so much to offer and can serve as a model for other schools and communities so that we can truly build back better." The Board invited Melanie Morey, principal of Barnard Elementary School, along with several Barnard staff members, to the podium to say a few words and receive congratulations and a certificate, then invited Dr. Erin Detmer, principal of Leonard Elementary School, along with several Leonard staff members, to do the same.

Additions & Deletions; Public Communication (Agenda Items)
Both recorded as None.

General - Consent Agenda, Resolution 21-085
It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Gottlieb that the Troy Board of Education take action to approve items A, B, C and D on the consent agenda: Minutes of the October 5, 2021 Board of Education Workshop; Minutes of the October 19, 2021 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report - September 2021; and Second Reading and Adoption of Board Policies, consisting of revisions to Policy 1000.02 Special Meetings and Policy 2000.06 Student Bullying, and the addition of a policy in Section 8000, Animals on District Property. The vote was Yes 7, No 0.

Personnel, Resolution 21-086
It was moved by Mrs. Hammond and supported by Dr. Wilson that the Board of Education approve the personnel recommendations as stated, identified in the minutes as New Hires: Aaron Ducharme and Toby Klein. The vote was Yes 7, No 0.

Curriculum
Recorded as None.

Business - Bus Purchase, Resolution 21-087
It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart that the bid for school buses be awarded to Hoekstra Transportation in the amount of $931,182.00 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2013 Bond Series 3. The vote was Yes 7, No 0.

Business - CAD Lab Computers, Resolution 21-088
It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne that the bid for CAD Lab Computers be awarded to Sehi Computer Products in the amount of $66,096 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2019 Capital Projects Fund and General Fund. The vote was Yes 7, No 0.

Reports from Student Representatives to the Board
Sasha Palmkoeck, student representative for Athens High School; Sarayu Bethamcherla, student representative for Troy High School; Alyssa McLarty, student representative for Troy College and Career High School; and Yara Mashal, student representative for International Academy-East, each shared a report on the events and activities happening in their schools.

Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items)
President Schmidt shared a statement providing the structure of how the evening's Public Participation would be conducted in compliance with the Open Meetings Act and reviewed the guidelines to be followed for public comment. Speakers were:

- Mrs. Kristina Gerami, TSD parent, on concerns about prejudice in the Troy School District and the struggles her child has had in school.
- Mrs. Katie MacFarland, TSD parent, on her dissatisfaction with how the book review of Fun Home was handled, and concerns about another book reviewed in 2015, What My Mother Doesn't Know, that is now available at Baker Middle School.
- Ms. Rebecca Han, TSD community member, on concerns with the District's summer reading AP English class and the suggested reading materials offered.
- Ms. Barbara Yagley, TSD community member, with concerns about graphic novels as grooming tools, stating that pedophiles have used these and that the Board are guardians who should not let that creep into the schools.
- Mrs. Diana Magiera, TSD parent, in opposition to the mask mandate, stating that leadership does not respect parents and describing the hostile environment it has created.
- B.J. Lennon, TSD parent, in opposition to the mask mandate in place in the Troy School District.
- Ryan Johnson, TSD parent, on diversity and equity and CRT and his opposition to the mask mandate; he demanded the immediate resignation of the superintendent and all Board members and threatened to sue each person for what he considers breaking the law, including the mask mandate, and unenrolling his son from school.
- Mr. Joe Thilman, Troy community member, in support of the mask mandate, thanking the Board for promoting concern for others and urging it to continue doing the right thing by working together.
- Stephanie Margilaj, TSD parent, on DEI and "the real crisis in the school system," discussing her concerns with the transformation of public education.
- Mr. Ollie Apahidean, TSD parent, on parental rights, displaying graphic pictures from a book found in the school library and discussing the book review committee.
- Heidi Fentress, TSD parent, in opposition to the mask mandate and also raising that her student was not able to use the bathrooms at Troy High during the day because they were closed.
- Sarah Krieger, TSD parent, in opposition to the mask mandate in the Troy School District.
- Mrs. Nahla Hassan, TSD parent, on special education services for her high school student and how children with disabilities have a right to FAPE.
- Mr. John Tyson, TSD community member, on focusing on education and not indoctrination.
- Mr. Daniel Kang, Athens High School graduate, on initiating a plan to change computer science classes to allow for more programming courses.

Other
Recorded as None.

Board Member Comments
Dr. Philippart shared that she attended the MASB conference the previous week and gave kudos to Karl Schmidt and Dr. Wilson for their work presenting the TSD Board Self-Evaluation tool, built off Michael Fullan's work. Mrs. Hammond shared that she attended the Troy College and Career High School PTO meeting and commented on how nice the building was. Mr. Gottlieb commented on Troy's participation in the NPDL Global Learning program and the great work being done with students. Mrs. Anne also commented on how insightful and useful the MASB Conference was. Mr. Hauff wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving and shared how grateful he is for the Board and Central Office administration. Dr. Wilson shared that she attended the Troy High play Pride & Prejudice and is excited to see Elf performed by the Athens Theatre Ensemble. Dr. Machesky indicated he is almost finished presenting the TSD Fall Update to staff and PTOs, sharing the challenges the District faces, and thanked the Board for their hard work and continued daily support. Mr. Schmidt shared that he and Dr. Wilson spent a half-day at the preschool for Trunk or Treat and mentioned how well everything functions at full capacity. He announced that the next Board Workshop would be held on Tuesday, December 7th at 6:00 p.m. at the Services Building and the next regular Board Meeting would be Tuesday, December 14th at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building.

Adjournment
The meeting adjourned at 8:38 p.m.
